Pyke.build: Build health first against Pyke’s physical damage and execute, then build armor. Armor improves Taric’s survivability as well as the damage of Taric E Dazzle and Taric P Bravado, so consider Frozen Heart or Randuin's Omen. There’s no reason to build magic resistance against this opponent.
Pyke.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to the ally who will engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance. Then stand apart from that ally and use Taric E Dazzle to block Pyke’s movement with its two stun areas. Follow with two empowered basic attacks from Taric P Bravado and heal your ally with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Taric R Cosmic Radiance activates with a delay, so it will be too late if you wait until Pyke R Death From Below puts an ally in danger.
Pyke.escape: Don’t push deep immediately after dodging the stun from Pyke E Phantom Undertow. If Pyke R Death From Below has also been used and hasn’t returned yet, that’s a chance to catch him with Taric E Dazzle and fight.
Pyke.fight: After dodging Pyke E Phantom Undertow to the side, predict where he’ll end up and cast Taric E Dazzle there. It’s a better opportunity to chase once Pyke R Death From Below has also been fully spent and is unavailable.
Pyke.laning: Don’t waste Taric E Dazzle on poke; use it to trade when Pyke steps up to last-hit a minion or engages first. After the trade, keep vision in the direction Pyke retreats so he can’t disappear from sight and heal. When using Taric P Bravado attacks on minions, target one with plenty of health so you don’t take your ADC’s last hit.
Pyke.phase: In the mid and late game, build armor and health to frontline, while also protecting the low-health allies Pyke targets.
Pyke.teamfight: When frontlining, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer to extend your protection, and use Taric R Cosmic Radiance early in anticipation of Pyke’s engage. Stuns still affect you while you’re invulnerable, so dodge the path of Pyke E Phantom Undertow and counter with Taric E Dazzle. When Pyke R Death From Below targets a low-health ally, don’t stand on top of them to prevent the execute chain.
Pyke.watch: If Pyke Q Bone Skewer pulls you in, Taric can’t escape on his own, so keep your distance. When Pyke E Phantom Undertow dashes, move to the side of the path he leaves behind to avoid the stun. If a shark shadow appears beneath your feet, Pyke W Ghostwater Dive is already close, so retreat toward an ally or turret.

Alistar.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to an ally who is about to engage, then cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance ahead of time. Use Taric E Dazzle, which also triggers from that ally's position, to look for a stun. Follow with two empowered basic attacks from Taric P Bravado, then heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Taric R Cosmic Radiance has a delay and doesn't prevent crowd control, so don't wait until Alistar has already caught you in his combo to cast it.
Alistar.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for your boots. Since Alistar Q Pulverize, Alistar W Headbutt, and Alistar E Trample deal magic damage, build magic resistance first to survive against him.
Alistar.escape: Alistar W Headbutt is his only mobility tool, so the moment you bait it out is your window to close the distance. If Alistar Q Pulverize is also down, counterattack with Taric E Dazzle. Until then, don't let him get close enough to catch you.
Alistar.fight: Open a trade with Taric E Dazzle just after Alistar W Headbutt and Alistar Q Pulverize are down. If the stun lands, follow your ability with two empowered basic attacks from Taric P Bravado to cycle your basic abilities faster.
Alistar.laning: Don't waste Taric E Dazzle on poke. Use it to predict Alistar's position when Alistar W Headbutt is down or when he steps up to last-hit. After a trade, use Taric P Bravado basic attacks on a high-health minion or another suitable target to expend them. If Taric Q Starlight's Touch isn't urgently needed, accumulate its charges and use them for healing.
Alistar.phase: In the mid and late game, armor also contributes to Taric's damage, but prioritize magic resistance to withstand Alistar's magic damage.
Alistar.teamfight: If Taric is on the frontline, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer so your abilities trigger from two positions. When Alistar R Unbreakable Will is active, don't focus your damage on him; back away and wait out its duration. If you can't retreat, interrupt Alistar's engage with Taric E Dazzle, and if the fight continues, target the damage dealer behind him.
Alistar.watch: Alistar W Headbutt and Alistar Q Pulverize can force-move and knock you up, followed by a stun from Alistar E Trample. Taric has no way to escape on his own, so manage the range Alistar needs to engage, and when defending a turret, don't leave room for him to flank.

Bard.watch: Bard Q Cosmic Binding stuns if it hits a wall or a second target, so don't stand with a wall behind you or in a line with an ally or minion. Watch for Bard E Magical Journey angles that let him approach from the side.
Bard.build: In the early game, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Bard deals mostly magic damage, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Bard.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to an ally who is about to engage, then cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance ahead of time. Make Taric E Dazzle activate from both positions. Follow with two empowered basic attacks from Taric P Bravado, then heal your ally with stored charges of Taric Q Starlight's Touch.
Bard.escape: The moment you bait out Bard E Magical Journey is your chance to engage, so go in then if Taric E Dazzle is ready. Avoid positions where Bard Q Cosmic Binding can stun you, and don't force an engage if Taric E Dazzle is unavailable.
Bard.fight: Close the distance just after Bard E Magical Journey is down and start a fight with Taric E Dazzle.
Bard.laning: Avoid the line formed by walls and allies or minions to avoid being stunned by Bard Q Cosmic Binding, and step on Bard W Caretaker's Shrine on the lane to remove it.
Bard.phase: In the mid and late game, stay on the frontline, and prepare for Bard's magic damage with magic resistance.
Bard.teamfight: When on the frontline, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer so your abilities trigger from two positions. Start a fight when Taric E Dazzle is ready, and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance before damage piles up so its delayed immunity overlaps with the fight.

Lulu.escape: The moment after Lulu W Whimsy is used on another ally is your chance to engage. Lulu has no dash to escape with, so after closing the distance, you can keep her in place by hitting Taric E Dazzle. When Lulu E Help, Pix! shields an ally and Pix is with an allied carry, target Lulu herself.
Lulu.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Lulu deals mostly magic damage, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Lulu.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to an ally who is about to engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance early. Then stun the spot Lulu is heading toward with Taric E Dazzle, hit twice with empowered Taric P Bravado attacks, and heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Standing slightly apart from the linked ally reduces Lulu’s room to dodge the two E beams.
Lulu.fight: Once Lulu W Whimsy has been used on another ally, close the distance and start a trade with Taric E Dazzle. E detonates after a delay, so aim for where Lulu will be standing shortly.
Lulu.laning: Stand behind minions to reduce the bonus damage from Lulu P Pix, Faerie Companion, and don’t step forward if you can’t start a trade with Taric E Dazzle. When you need Taric P Bravado attacks, choose a high-health minion so you don’t take your ADC’s last hit. If it isn’t urgent, save charges on Taric Q Starlight's Touch to heal several allies at once.
Lulu.phase: In the mid and late game, armor items contribute to both Taric’s frontline role and damage, but prioritize resistance against Lulu’s magic damage.
Lulu.teamfight: When Taric stands in front, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer so abilities trigger from both positions. Cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance early to account for its delay before damage comes in, and watch for Lulu R Wild Growth to lock down your allies with its knockup. If Lulu R Wild Growth is ready, don’t fixate on the protected target; go for Lulu or another target.
Lulu.watch: Lulu W Whimsy silences you and prevents you from attacking, so don’t engage while it’s ready. Lulu Q Glitterlance’s slow and Lulu R Wild Growth’s knockup can also lock you down; Taric R Cosmic Radiance doesn’t stop crowd control. If Lulu R Wild Growth is ready, don’t dive deep assuming its protected target is a guaranteed kill.

Brand.phase: In the mid and late game against Brand, prioritize magic resistance over armor, and keep your distance so his area damage doesn't spread.
Brand.watch: While you are affected by Brand P Blaze, Brand Q Sear stuns you if it hits, so dodge the projectile or hide behind minions. Dodging Brand W Pillar of Flame first also makes it easier to avoid the follow-up stacks. When you see Brand R Pyroclasm, spread out from your allies to reduce its bounces.
Brand.build: In the early game, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Brand deals mostly magic damage, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Brand.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to an ally who is about to engage, then cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance ahead of time and hit with Taric E Dazzle from both positions. Follow with two empowered basic attacks from Taric P Bravado, then heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Taric R Cosmic Radiance activates late, so use it before Brand's follow-up attacks arrive.
Brand.escape: The moment Brand W Pillar of Flame is down is your chance to close the distance. If you're burning, first dodge the stun from Brand Q Sear, then engage with Taric E Dazzle. Brand has no mobility, so once you get close, it's hard for him to create distance.
Brand.fight: When Brand W Pillar of Flame is down and Brand remains in range, engage with Taric E Dazzle. If the stun lands, follow your ability with two empowered basic attacks from Taric P Bravado to cycle your basic abilities faster, then heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch.
Brand.laning: Stand to the side of the wave because Brand E Conflagration can spread from burning minions. If Taric E Dazzle is unavailable or there's no position to land it, don't walk forward into poke. When using basic attacks to expend Taric P Bravado, choose a high-health minion so you don't take your marksman's last-hit.
Brand.teamfight: If an ally is burning, don't stand next to them. Spread out before engaging so Brand E Conflagration and Brand R Pyroclasm don't spread. Link Taric W Bastion to an ally on the side where you aren't standing to widen the stun coverage of Taric E Dazzle.

Morgana.watch: Morgana Q Dark Binding catches the first target it hits, so avoid it with a minion between you and Morgana. If Morgana R Soul Shackles connects, move out of range before the stun triggers.
Morgana.build: Early on, weather the lane with a Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Morgana deals mostly magic damage, so build magic resistance first. If a long fight makes healing from Morgana P Soul Siphon and Morgana W Tormented Shadow a problem, consider anti-heal next.
Morgana.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to the ally who will engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance. Cast Taric E Dazzle along the movement path of a target whose Morgana E Black Shield is down, then land two P Bravado attacks and heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Taric R Cosmic Radiance blocks damage but not roots or stuns, so keep dodging the angles of Morgana Q Dark Binding.
Morgana.escape: Dodge Morgana Q Dark Binding; when Morgana E Black Shield is down, you have a chance to engage. Morgana has no spell to create distance on her own, so close in and catch her with Taric E Dazzle.
Morgana.fight: Dodge Morgana Q Dark Binding and close the distance when Morgana E Black Shield is down. Taric E Dazzle detonates with a delay, so cast it where your opponent will be shortly. After hitting it, land two P Bravado attacks after each ability to cycle your basic abilities faster. Use Taric W Bastion’s shield and Taric Q Starlight's Touch’s healing when trading damage.
Morgana.laning: Keep minions between you and Morgana to reduce the angles Morgana Q Dark Binding can reach you from. Don’t move forward if you can’t start a trade with Taric E Dazzle, and don’t waste a stun on a target protected by Morgana E Black Shield. Use P Bravado attacks on a minion with plenty of health, and dodge Morgana W Tormented Shadow’s pool when retreating.
Morgana.phase: In the mid and late game, prioritize magic resistance against Morgana. As Taric builds armor items, his frontline presence and damage contribution both increase.
Morgana.teamfight: When frontlining, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer to extend your shield and spell range. Avoid the angles of Morgana Q Dark Binding as you engage with Taric E Dazzle, and account for Taric R Cosmic Radiance’s delay by casting it before the fight. Morgana R Soul Shackles can stun you even while you’re invulnerable, so if the tether connects, move out of range before it detonates.

Blitzcrank.build: In the early game, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab and Blitzcrank R Static Field deal mostly magic damage, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Blitzcrank.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to an ally who is about to engage, then cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance ahead of time and look for a stun with Taric E Dazzle. Stand slightly apart from your linked ally so the two Taric E Dazzle casts cover different areas. After the stun, follow with two empowered basic attacks from Taric P Bravado, then heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch.
Blitzcrank.escape: Engage just after Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses or when he lacks the mana to use his hook. Blitzcrank has no ability to create distance on his own, so if you get an angle to catch him, look for a stun with Taric E Dazzle.
Blitzcrank.fight: Start a fight when Taric E Dazzle is ready, and follow a landed stun with two empowered basic attacks from Taric P Bravado. If it isn't urgent, save charges of Taric Q Starlight's Touch to heal several allies at once. The moment Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses is your chance to step forward and trade.
Blitzcrank.laning: Stand behind minions so Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab hits a minion first, and keep an eye on Blitzcrank's mana. After Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses, gain an advantage by pushing the lane or trading. When using Taric P Bravado basic attacks on minions, choose a high-health minion so you don't take your marksman's last-hit.
Blitzcrank.phase: In the early game, one hit from Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab can make it easy to get caught by chained crowd control, so manage your distance first. In the mid and late game, stacking armor items improves both Taric's frontline role and his damage contribution.
Blitzcrank.watch: If Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab pulls you in, it can be followed by the knock-up from Blitzcrank E Power Fist and the silence from Blitzcrank R Static Field. Stand behind minions, and keep away from bushes when you don't have vision inside them. Taric R Cosmic Radiance prevents damage but not crowd control, so cast it just before the fight rather than after you've been grabbed.
Blitzcrank.teamfight: If Taric is on the frontline, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer and cast your abilities from two positions. Anticipate crowd control from Blitzcrank chaining onto an ally and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance ahead of time, while accounting for the fact that allies can still be caught during the damage immunity. Don't focus only on attacking Blitzcrank; use Taric E Dazzle to find a fight angle that reaches allies at the rear.

Braum.build: Use a Null-Magic Mantle to hold on in the early game, then choose Mercury's Treads. Braum's main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first, but tenacity is also important since Taric has no ability to escape.
Braum.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to an ally who is about to engage, then cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance ahead of time and look for a stun with Taric E Dazzle. Follow with two empowered basic attacks, then heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Taric R Cosmic Radiance activates late, so cast it before the fight starts, not after it becomes dangerous.
Braum.escape: The moment Braum W Stand Behind Me is down is your chance to close the distance and land Taric E Dazzle. If you're marked by Braum P Concussive Blows or need to dodge Braum R Glacial Fissure, create distance first and look for an angle again afterward.
Braum.fight: Start a trade when Taric E Dazzle is ready, and if the stun lands, follow your ability with two empowered basic attacks to cycle your basic abilities faster. Don't extend a trade while marked by Braum P Concussive Blows; back away.
Braum.laning: Don't face Braum in a straight line; dodge Braum Q Winter's Bite from behind minions. Use Taric E Dazzle when Braum steps up to last-hit, and after a trade, use two basic attacks on a high-health minion to speed up your ability rotation.
Braum.phase: In the mid and late game, build armor items to improve both your frontline role and damage contribution, but target the person Braum is protecting rather than focusing your damage on him.
Braum.teamfight: If you're on the frontline, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer to cover two positions with your abilities. Allies' projectiles are blocked in front of Braum E Unbreakable, so fight when his shield drops or you have an angle from the side. Taric R Cosmic Radiance prevents damage but not crowd control, so time it while dodging the line of Braum R Glacial Fissure.
Braum.watch: Dodge Braum Q Winter's Bite from behind minions, and if Braum P Concussive Blows marks you, create distance before stun stacks build up. Watch Braum R Glacial Fissure's cast and dodge sideways out of its line; also avoid the slow field it leaves behind.

Heimerdinger.build: In the early game, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Heimerdinger's main damage is magic, and Taric has low magic resistance, so prioritize magic resistance.
Heimerdinger.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to an ally who is about to engage, then cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance ahead of time. Follow with Taric E Dazzle to look for a stun, two basic attacks from Taric P Bravado, then heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Stand a little apart from your linked ally to spread out the stun coverage from both positions.
Heimerdinger.escape: Heimerdinger has no mobility, so you can catch him by going around his turret setup to close the distance, then landing Taric E Dazzle.
Heimerdinger.fight: After stunning with Taric E Dazzle, follow with two basic attacks from Taric P Bravado to cycle your basic abilities faster.
Heimerdinger.laning: Don't lose health trying to last-hit within turret range; wait at a safe distance. Don't waste Taric E Dazzle on poke. Use it to start a fight when the grenade is down and you can engage. If there's no chance to get close and catch him, put pressure on another lane instead of forcing yourself to hold this one.
Heimerdinger.phase: In the mid and late game, take the frontline role while continuing to prioritize resistance against Heimerdinger's magic damage and routes around his turret setup.
Heimerdinger.teamfight: If Taric is on the frontline, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer so your abilities reach from two positions. While Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! is available, don't group up in tight spaces in front of objectives.
Heimerdinger.watch: While Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! is ready, don't group up in tight spaces because of his empowered grenade.

Hwei.build: In the early game, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Hwei deals mostly magic damage, so build magic resistance first, and get tenacity to prepare for the root or forced movement from Hwei E Subject: Torment.
Hwei.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to an ally who is about to engage, then cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance ahead of time and aim Taric E Dazzle in Hwei's direction of movement. After the stun, follow with two empowered basic attacks from Taric P Bravado, then heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Taric R Cosmic Radiance activates late, so start early enough for its damage immunity to overlap with the trade after the stun ends.
Hwei.escape: Close the distance while Hwei E Subject: Torment is down. Hwei has no mobility, so if you reach him, you'll have a chance to land Taric E Dazzle. If Hwei E Subject: Torment is still available, wait; your engage's lead player could be sent back or rooted.
Hwei.fight: The moment Hwei E Subject: Torment is used for poke or wave clear is your chance to engage. Link an engaging ally with Taric W Bastion, and pre-aim Taric E Dazzle at where Hwei will move.
Hwei.laning: Don't waste Taric E Dazzle on poke; use it to start a trade. If Hwei E Subject: Torment has left an eye behind, change your gank path or put a minion or something else in front to trigger it first. After a trade, expend two basic attacks from Taric P Bravado on a high-health minion so you don't take a last-hit.
Hwei.phase: In the mid and late game, choose your engage when Hwei E Subject: Torment is down, and take a wide route around the areas Hwei has set up.
Hwei.teamfight: If Taric is on the frontline, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer so Taric E Dazzle and Taric R Cosmic Radiance activate from two positions. Open the engage with a stun after Hwei E Subject: Torment is down, and account for Taric R Cosmic Radiance's delay by casting it before damage piles up. Crowd control still works during damage immunity, so time the engage to avoid leaving allies caught while it runs.
Hwei.watch: If you get caught by the root or forced movement from Hwei E Subject: Torment, follow-up attacks are likely, so don't lead the engage while this ability is available. If the first ability hits, move immediately to avoid the second ability and the explosion from Hwei P Signature of the Visionary. Hwei Q Subject: Disaster can deal damage based on maximum or missing health, and Hwei R Spiraling Despair slows you, so don't stay in the area it telegraphs.

Janna.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Janna deals mostly magic damage, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Janna.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to an ally who is about to engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance early. Then stand slightly apart from that ally and aim Taric E Dazzle’s two beams at Janna. If the stun lands, hit twice with Taric P Bravado’s empowered attacks and heal your ally with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Focus damage on a target protected by Janna E Eye Of The Storm once the shield is gone.
Janna.escape: Look for an opening to engage with Taric E Dazzle after Janna Q Howling Gale misses. If Janna R Monsoon is down, there’s also less risk of being knocked back. Account for the movement speed from Janna W Zephyr by aiming Taric E Dazzle where Janna will be shortly, rather than where she is now.
Janna.fight: Open a trade when Taric E Dazzle is ready and you’ve dodged Janna Q Howling Gale. When Janna steps up to last-hit a minion, cast Taric E Dazzle ahead of time toward where she’ll be standing shortly.
Janna.laning: If there’s no opening for Taric E Dazzle, don’t step forward and take Janna’s ranged poke. Pressure the ally Janna is protecting to draw out Janna E Eye Of The Storm, then target someone without a shield. After a trade, use two Taric P Bravado attacks on a high-health minion, but don’t take your allied ADC’s last hit.
Janna.phase: In the mid and late game, armor items improve both Taric’s frontline role and damage contribution, but keep accounting for the knockback from Janna R Monsoon.
Janna.teamfight: When Taric stands in front, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer so abilities can trigger from both positions. While Janna stays behind her damage dealers to stop your engage, secure vision and look for a moment when she’s isolated. Cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance early to account for its delay, and avoid the path of Janna Q Howling Gale, since its knockup still works during damage immunity.
Janna.watch: Janna Q Howling Gale knocks up, so if you hear its tornado from a brush or out of vision, avoid its path. If Janna W Zephyr slows you, it becomes harder to close in with Taric E Dazzle. Janna R Monsoon knocks away enemies who engage, so don’t dive relying only on the damage immunity from Taric R Cosmic Radiance.

Karma.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Karma’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first.
Karma.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to an ally who is about to engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance early. Then stun with Taric E Dazzle, hit twice with Taric P Bravado, and heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Time your engage for when the shield from Karma E Inspire expires, and account for the delay on Taric R Cosmic Radiance.
Karma.escape: Engage after Karma W Focused Resolve is down and the shield and movement speed from Karma E Inspire have expired. If Karma W Focused Resolve tethers you, move out of range to break the tether before it roots you.
Karma.fight: Bait out Karma W Focused Resolve or break its tether, then engage after the shield from Karma E Inspire expires. Open the fight with a stun from Taric E Dazzle, then use two Taric P Bravado attacks after your abilities to cycle your basic abilities faster.
Karma.laning: Don’t use Taric E Dazzle for poke; save it as an engage when Karma steps up to last-hit a minion. If there’s no opening to land the stun, don’t step forward; reposition so Karma’s abilities won’t hit. After a fight, when using Taric P Bravado attacks on minions, choose high-health targets so you don’t take your allied ADC’s last hit.
Karma.phase: In the mid and late game, link allies with Taric W Bastion and serve as the frontline.
Karma.teamfight: Bait out Karma W Focused Resolve first, then start a fight after the shield from Karma E Inspire empowered by Karma R Mantra expires. When Taric stands in front, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer to extend your ability range. Use Taric R Cosmic Radiance ahead of the moment you need damage immunity, and account for the fact that it won’t stop roots.
Karma.watch: Watch out for the slow from Karma Q Inner Flame and the root from Karma W Focused Resolve. Taric has no ability to escape on his own, so keep your distance. If you’re hit by the area left by Karma Q Inner Flame empowered by Karma R Mantra, leave the circle immediately.

Leona.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Leona deals mostly magic damage, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Later, also consider the damage type of the enemy carry dealing damage while Leona holds you in place when choosing resistances.
Leona.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to an ally who is about to engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance early, then look for a stun with Taric E Dazzle. Follow with two empowered Taric P Bravado attacks and heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Leona’s crowd control still works during the damage immunity from Taric R Cosmic Radiance, so account for its delay to keep your allies from being locked down when the invulnerability activates.
Leona.escape: The moment right after you bait Leona E Zenith Blade is your window to close the distance. If you use Taric E Dazzle then, it’s harder for Leona to get away, but she may have Leona Q Shield of Daybreak active already, so watch both your engage range and your allies’ positions.
Leona.fight: Look for a stun with Taric E Dazzle just after Leona E Zenith Blade is down. If it lands, follow your abilities with two empowered Taric P Bravado attacks to cycle your basic abilities faster. Save charges on Taric Q Starlight's Touch for healing when it isn’t urgent.
Leona.laning: Don’t stand in line with your ranged carry, so Leona E Zenith Blade can’t reach a farther target. Leona can approach with Leona Q Shield of Daybreak already active, so judge safety by distance rather than whether she has used an ability. Don’t waste Taric E Dazzle on poke; use it to start a fight or counter Leona’s engage.
Leona.phase: In the mid and late game, Taric’s armor helps with both frontline duties and damage, so choose resistances based on the damage from Leona and the enemy carry.
Leona.teamfight: When Taric stands in front, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer so Taric E Dazzle and Taric R Cosmic Radiance trigger from both positions. If Leona P Sunlight marks you, that signals enemy damage is coming, so don’t move farther forward; back off. Cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance early enough to block the damage, and account for the fact that it won’t stop crowd control.
Leona.watch: If Leona E Zenith Blade hits you, she can dash in and follow up with the crowd control from Leona Q Shield of Daybreak and Leona R Solar Flare, so don’t let her get close enough to engage first. When Leona W Eclipse is active, get out of range before it explodes. If the indicator for Leona R Solar Flare appears, move to the side to avoid the center stun.

Lux.build: Early on, weather the lane with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Lux’s main damage is magic, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Lux.combo: After Lux Q Light Binding misses, link an ally who is about to engage with Taric W Bastion and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance early. Then stun Lux with Taric E Dazzle, hit twice with Taric P Bravado, and heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Account for R’s delay so the invulnerability overlaps the trade after the stun.
Lux.escape: Close the distance during the window when Lux Q Light Binding is down. Lux has no ability to create distance on her own, so once you’re close, it’s hard for her to get away if Taric E Dazzle hits.
Lux.fight: The moment after you dodge Lux Q Light Binding is your chance to engage. Link an ally with Taric W Bastion and cast Taric E Dazzle ahead of time toward where Lux will move.
Lux.laning: If you can’t start a trade with Taric E Dazzle, don’t step forward into Lux’s poke. Use Taric P Bravado attacks on minions that aren’t close to dying to cycle your abilities, and save charges on Taric Q Starlight's Touch for healing if it isn’t urgent.
Lux.phase: In the mid and late game, stand on the frontline and extend your abilities’ range to allies with W’s tether.
Lux.teamfight: Approach from a different direction instead of grouping with allies, so you don’t all get caught by Lux E Lucent Singularity. When Taric stands in front, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer so your abilities trigger from both positions.
Lux.watch: Lux Q Light Binding roots up to the first two enemies it hits, and if it hits you, it becomes harder to dodge her follow-up abilities. Don’t stand in line with your ally; bait out and dodge Q, then reposition. Leave the area where Lux E Lucent Singularity is placed, and sidestep when you see the aim line for Lux R Final Spark.

Maokai.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Build magic resistance first to counter Maokai’s main damage. Maokai Q Bramble Smash deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid choices that only add a lot of health.
Maokai.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to an ally who is about to engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance early. After Maokai W Twisted Advance ends, aim Taric E Dazzle at the expected landing spot, then hit twice with empowered Taric P Bravado attacks and heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Taric R Cosmic Radiance activates after a delay, so don’t wait until the fight becomes dangerous.
Maokai.escape: The moment after Maokai W Twisted Advance is down is Taric’s window to engage. If Maokai R Nature's Grasp is also ready, fight in open terrain where you have room to dodge the root.
Maokai.fight: Close the distance just after Maokai W Twisted Advance is down. Cast Taric E Dazzle ahead of time toward where Maokai will move after landing. If the stun hits, use two empowered Taric P Bravado attacks to reduce your basic abilities’ cooldowns. Repeatedly hitting Maokai with abilities brings Maokai P Sap Magic’s healing back sooner, so avoid pointless poke.
Maokai.laning: While Maokai W Twisted Advance is ready, stay out of range near brush, and use the moment after it’s down to trade. Don’t waste Taric E Dazzle on poke; use it to start a fight. If you have Taric P Bravado attacks left after the trade, use them on a high-health minion so you don’t interfere with your allied ADC’s last hit.
Maokai.phase: In the mid and late game, extend your abilities’ range to allies with Taric W Bastion, while staying alert for Maokai’s roots and magic damage.
Maokai.teamfight: When Taric stands in front, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer so abilities trigger from both positions. If Maokai R Nature's Grasp comes, move to the side in open terrain, and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance before the damage arrives. Maokai’s root still works during damage immunity, so time the engage to keep your allies from spending the invulnerability while rooted.
Maokai.watch: Maokai W Twisted Advance dashes in and roots, so don’t close the distance near brush while it’s ready. Don’t enter brush where Maokai E Sapling Toss has planted a sapling. If Maokai R Nature's Grasp comes from far away, dodge perpendicular to its direction. Taric R Cosmic Radiance’s damage immunity doesn’t stop roots, so move before you’re rooted.

Milio.build: Early on, first weather the lane with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Milio deals magic damage, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Choose later resistances based on the enemy carry’s damage type. If the healing from Milio W Cozy Campfire and Milio R Breath of Life becomes a problem, get anti-heal earlier.
Milio.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to an ally who is about to engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance early, then look for a stun with Taric E Dazzle. Follow with two empowered Taric P Bravado attacks and heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Standing slightly apart from the linked ally lets Taric E Dazzle’s beams from both positions reduce Milio’s room to dodge.
Milio.escape: The moment Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is down is your window to engage. It’s Milio’s only way to disengage, knocking back the first enemy he hits, so close the distance and land Taric E Dazzle after it’s used.
Milio.fight: After Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is down, close the distance and start a fight with Taric E Dazzle. Taric E Dazzle detonates late, so aim where Milio will be shortly. Once you’re close, use your abilities and hit twice with Taric P Bravado’s empowered attacks to speed up your basic ability rotation.
Milio.laning: If there’s no opening to start a fight with Taric E Dazzle, don’t step forward into poke. When using basic attacks to consume Taric P Bravado, choose a high-health minion so you don’t take your ADC’s last hit. If it isn’t urgent, accumulate charges before using Taric Q Starlight's Touch.
Milio.phase: Milio’s team gets stronger over time, so drain mana through trades during the laning phase and take control of the wave.
Milio.teamfight: If you can reach Milio himself, target him first to cut off the enemy team’s sustain. When Taric stands on the frontline, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer to extend your ability range to two positions. Taric R Cosmic Radiance activates late, so cast it early just before a fight or right after using Taric E Dazzle.
Milio.watch: Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick knocks back the first enemy it hits and applies an area slow, which can stop Taric’s engage. Delay frontline fights while Milio W Cozy Campfire is active and the enemy ADC has increased range. Also account for the shield and movement speed from Milio E Warm Hugs when engaging.

Nami.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Nami deals mostly magic damage, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so prioritize building magic resistance.
Nami.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to an ally who is about to engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance early. Then stun Nami with Taric E Dazzle, trigger Taric P Bravado with two basic attacks, and heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Standing slightly apart from the linked ally lets Taric E Dazzle from both positions threaten a wider area.
Nami.escape: Close the distance and engage just after Nami Q Aqua Prison misses. Nami has no mobility ability, so if you get close, you can hold her in place with Taric E Dazzle. When Nami R Tidal Wave appears, dodge to the side first to avoid the crowd control that follows.
Nami.fight: The moment after Nami Q Aqua Prison misses is your chance to start a trade with Taric E Dazzle. Taric E Dazzle detonates late, so aim for where Nami will be standing shortly.
Nami.laning: If Taric E Dazzle isn’t ready or there’s no opening to land it, don’t step forward into poke. Secure vision and line up an angle toward Nami, but engage after Nami Q Aqua Prison is down. After a trade, use two Taric P Bravado attacks on a high-health minion or similar target to cycle your basic abilities faster.
Nami.phase: In the mid and late game, Taric’s armor also contributes to damage, but prioritize magic resistance to withstand Nami’s magic damage.
Nami.teamfight: Link Taric W Bastion to an ally who is away from you to extend the reach of Taric E Dazzle and Taric R Cosmic Radiance. Cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance early, accounting for its delay, before an ally is caught by Nami R Tidal Wave or Nami Q Aqua Prison. Crowd control still works during invulnerability, so move to the side of an indicated area.
Nami.watch: Nami Q Aqua Prison stuns but falls slowly, so sidestep when you see it coming. Nami R Tidal Wave also approaches slowly, and the crowd control that follows can be dangerous if it hits, so move to the side as soon as you see it. Avoid trading head-on with someone affected by Nami E Tidecaller's Blessing until its duration ends.

Nautilus.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Nautilus deals mostly magic damage, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Nautilus.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to the ally who will engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance. Use Taric E Dazzle in the window after Nautilus Q Dredge Line has been used. If the stun lands, hit two empowered attacks from Taric P Bravado, then heal your ally with Taric Q Starlight's Touch.
Nautilus.escape: The window to engage is right after Nautilus Q Dredge Line misses. Stun him with Taric E Dazzle then, finish the trade, and move out of basic attack range so you don’t get rooted by Nautilus P Staggering Blow.
Nautilus.fight: Open a trade with Taric E Dazzle right after Nautilus Q Dredge Line misses. E detonates with a delay, so aim where Nautilus will be. After hitting it, land two empowered basic attacks from Taric P Bravado after each ability to cycle your basic abilities faster.
Nautilus.laning: Manage your distance with minions between you and Nautilus to block Nautilus Q Dredge Line, and don’t waste Taric E Dazzle on poke. When using Taric P Bravado attacks on minions, target one with plenty of health so you don’t take your ADC’s last hit.
Nautilus.phase: In the mid and late game, build armor to contribute damage while serving as the frontline, but against this opponent, prioritize magic resistance.
Nautilus.teamfight: When frontlining, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer so Taric E Dazzle and Taric R Cosmic Radiance activate from two positions. Taric R Cosmic Radiance takes time to apply and does not prevent crowd control, so cast it early in anticipation of Nautilus’s engage. Don’t stand on top of an ally in the path of Nautilus R Depth Charge.
Nautilus.watch: Nautilus Q Dredge Line starts fights with a stun and a dash. If you are also hit by the root from Nautilus P Staggering Blow that follows, Taric has no mobility spell and has difficulty escaping. Dodge Q by keeping minions between you, and if Nautilus R Depth Charge is ready, avoid overlapping with allies along the engage path.

Pantheon.build: Pantheon deals mostly physical damage, so build armor first and consider high-armor items such as Frozen Heart or Randuin's Omen. Bonus armor also increases the damage of Taric E Dazzle and Taric P Bravado. However, Pantheon W Shield Vault deals damage based on your maximum health, and Pantheon R Grand Starfall has armor penetration, so don’t assume health or armor alone will cover all his damage.
Pantheon.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to the ally who will engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance, then look for a stun with Taric E Dazzle. Follow with two empowered basic attacks from Taric P Bravado and heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. While Pantheon E Aegis Assault blocks damage from the front, change your attack angle or wait for it to end. Account for the fact that Taric R Cosmic Radiance’s invulnerability doesn’t block the stun from Pantheon W Shield Vault.
Pantheon.escape: The window to engage is after Pantheon W Shield Vault has been used and before Pantheon R Grand Starfall comes back up. Don’t engage first from within range of Pantheon W Shield Vault’s stun.
Pantheon.fight: Open with Taric E Dazzle when Pantheon E Aegis Assault ends or you have an angle from the side, then follow each spell with two empowered basic attacks from Taric P Bravado. Avoid situations where you get stunned first within Pantheon W Shield Vault’s range.
Pantheon.laning: Keep minions between you and Pantheon during his Pantheon Q Comet Spear poke to reduce the damage you take. Don’t waste Taric E Dazzle on poke; use it to start a trade when an opening appears, such as when Pantheon steps up to last-hit a minion. When using Taric P Bravado attacks on minions, target one with plenty of health so you don’t take your ADC’s last hit.
Pantheon.phase: In the late game, Pantheon’s influence falls off, while Taric can build armor items to increase both his durability and damage, so buy time while fighting.
Pantheon.teamfight: When frontlining, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer so spells activate from two positions. If you expect Pantheon to engage, cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance early enough to account for its delay, and look for a stun with Taric E Dazzle. Taric R Cosmic Radiance only blocks damage, so casting it after Pantheon W Shield Vault stuns an ally makes it difficult to get full use of the invulnerability.
Pantheon.watch: Pantheon W Shield Vault stuns a targeted enemy, so don’t give him range to use it. When Pantheon uses Q Comet Spear to poke, keep minions between you. If Pantheon E Aegis Assault is active, stop attacking from the front and wait for it to end, or angle in from the side. If you see the landing warning for Pantheon R Grand Starfall, walk out of its landing area.

Rakan.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Rakan deals mostly magic damage, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Rakan.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to the ally who will engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance. Then use Taric E Dazzle along Rakan’s movement path, trigger Taric P Bravado with two basic attacks, and heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Taric R Cosmic Radiance blocks damage but not charms or knock-ups, so account for its delay when casting.
Rakan.escape: Dodge the landing of Rakan W Grand Entrance; the window to engage is right after he uses it. If Rakan is separated from his allies, he can’t dash to them with Rakan E Battle Dance, so predict his movement path and land Taric E Dazzle.
Rakan.fight: Start a trade just after Rakan P Fey Feathers’ shield is removed and Rakan W Grand Entrance has been used. Cast Taric E Dazzle where Rakan will be shortly, and after it hits, use two basic attacks to take advantage of Taric P Bravado each time you cast a spell.
Rakan.laning: Taric has no spell to escape on his own, so manage your distance to avoid getting caught at once by Rakan W Grand Entrance and Rakan R The Quickness. Don’t move forward if there’s no opening to start a trade with Taric E Dazzle. After a trade, choose a minion with plenty of health and use up Taric P Bravado’s empowered basic attacks to bring your basic abilities back up sooner.
Rakan.phase: In the mid and late game, keep your distance with Rakan’s crowd control in mind, and use Taric W Bastion to extend your spell range to an ally.
Rakan.teamfight: When Taric is frontlining, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer so spells activate from two positions. Aim Taric E Dazzle in advance at where Rakan will engage with Rakan W Grand Entrance, and don’t stand in a line with allies where Rakan R The Quickness can reach several of you. Account for Taric R Cosmic Radiance’s delay and cast it before damage pours in.
Rakan.watch: Rakan W Grand Entrance’s landing point is visible, so sidestep when his dash starts to avoid the knock-up. When Rakan R The Quickness is active, don’t stand in a line with allies, and block his path with Taric E Dazzle before he reaches you.

Rell.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Rell deals mostly magic damage, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Rell.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to the ally who will engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance, then look for a stun with Taric E Dazzle, which also activates at your ally’s position. Follow with two basic attacks to take advantage of Taric P Bravado and heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch.
Rell.escape: Don’t engage just because Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down is down; wait until she has also used Rell E Full Tilt. Rell has difficulty escaping if you land Taric E Dazzle before Rell E Full Tilt comes back up.
Rell.fight: Wait outside the range of Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down, then engage with Taric E Dazzle before Rell E Full Tilt comes back up.
Rell.laning: If Rell runs quickly toward Taric, give up on trading and retreat outside the range of Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down.
Rell.teamfight: Spread out before the engage so Rell R Magnet Storm doesn’t pull several allies together. While frontlining, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer, cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance early in anticipation of Rell’s engage, then look for a stun with Taric E Dazzle.
Rell.watch: If Rell E Full Tilt speeds up Rell and one ally together, that signals she’ll engage with Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down, so retreat out of range. Rell Q Shattering Strike breaks shields, so dodge it to the side and use Taric W Bastion’s shield after Rell Q Shattering Strike has been used.

Renata.build: Early on, weather the lane with a Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Renata Glasc deals mostly magic damage, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Renata Glasc P Leverage scales with maximum health, so avoid builds that add a large amount of health alone.
Renata.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to the ally who will engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance. Then stun Renata Glasc with Taric E Dazzle, follow with two Taric P Bravado attacks, and heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Standing slightly apart from the linked ally narrows Renata Glasc’s room to dodge Taric E Dazzle cast from two positions.
Renata.escape: The window to close in and engage is after Renata Glasc Q Handshake has been used. Renata Glasc has no mobility spell of her own, so if you land Taric E Dazzle after getting close, she’ll have difficulty escaping. Keep your distance from allies when engaging in a fight while Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is ready.
Renata.fight: Start a fight with Taric E Dazzle when Renata Glasc Q Handshake is down and you can close the distance. After landing the stun, hit two attacks sped up by Taric P Bravado, and heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch when needed. If you kill an enemy affected by Renata Glasc W Bailout, move away so an ally doesn’t die near them.
Renata.laning: Renata Glasc has no mobility spell of her own, so pressure her when you have an angle to get close. Taric E Dazzle detonates with a delay, so cast it in advance, timing it for the moment Renata Glasc steps up to last-hit a minion. While you can’t start a fight with Taric E Dazzle, don’t move forward and take poke.
Renata.phase: In the mid and late game, armor items contribute to Taric’s frontline role and damage, but magic resistance is the first resistance you need against Renata Glasc.
Renata.teamfight: When Taric is frontlining, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer to extend the positions where spells activate. While Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is ready, don’t engage grouped together in a line with allies. In fights where Taric E Dazzle is ready, account for Taric R Cosmic Radiance’s delay and cast it in advance. Right after killing an enemy affected by Renata Glasc W Bailout, retreat so an ally doesn’t go down.
Renata.watch: Renata Glasc Q Handshake roots the first target it hits and throws them, potentially stunning an ally too, so dodge it by standing behind minions or the frontline. If hit by Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover, you’ll attack your allies, so keep your distance from them in fights while R is ready. Taric R Cosmic Radiance blocks damage but not crowd control, so adjust your position before being hit by Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover.

Senna.build: Senna’s main damage is physical, so build armor first. Consider armor-heavy items such as Frozen Heart or Randuin’s Omen. Armor improves both Taric’s survivability and the damage of Taric E Dazzle and Taric P Bravado.
Senna.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to the ally who will engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance. Then aim Taric E Dazzle at the spot where Senna will be a moment later, hit two basic attacks from Taric P Bravado, and heal with Taric Q Starlight’s Touch. Standing slightly apart from your linked ally lets you aim the two beams from Taric E Dazzle over a wider area.
Senna.escape: After Senna W Last Embrace is blocked by a minion or misses, Senna stepping forward to collect a soul is an opportunity to engage. Senna has no spell to create distance on her own, so close the gap and lock her down with Taric E Dazzle. However, if you see an enemy approaching using Senna E Curse of the Black Mist, don’t fight there; retreat to an area where you have vision.
Senna.fight: Look for an engage when Senna steps forward to collect a soul, starting the fight with Taric E Dazzle. After stunning her, hit two empowered basic attacks from Taric P Bravado and heal with Taric Q Starlight’s Touch. If there’s no angle to reach her with Taric E Dazzle, don’t step forward and take poke.
Senna.laning: Watch the soul locations and pressure the spots Senna approaches to collect them. Avoid the straight path of Senna Q Piercing Darkness, and block Senna W Last Embrace from behind minions. After a trade, when using Taric P Bravado’s basic attacks on minions, choose a high-health target so you don’t take a last hit from your allied marksman.
Senna.phase: In the mid game, use Taric R Cosmic Radiance to respond to enemy engages or dives. In the late game, watch out for Senna’s range and attack damage growth from collecting souls while making use of Taric’s role as a frontline with stacked armor and his damage contribution.
Senna.teamfight: When you see Senna E Curse of the Black Mist, back off to secure vision and watch for enemies approaching through the mist. When Taric stands in front, link Taric W Bastion to a backline ally to create two points from which your abilities can reach. Use Taric R Cosmic Radiance just before the fight or just after Taric E Dazzle, not after damage has landed, and keep in mind that it won’t block Senna W Last Embrace’s root even while you’re invulnerable.
Senna.watch: Senna Q Piercing Darkness passes through allies or minions to slow enemies and heal allies, so move out of the line between Senna and her target. Dodge Senna W Last Embrace from behind minions, and if it hits you, move away from your allies before the root spreads. After Senna hits you once, back off to prevent her from attacking again and collecting mist.

Seraphine.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Seraphine’s damage is mostly magic, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Seraphine.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to the ally who will engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance, then stun Seraphine with Taric E Dazzle. Follow up with two basic attacks empowered by Taric P Bravado and heal with Taric Q Starlight’s Touch. Account for the delayed activation of Taric R Cosmic Radiance’s damage immunity and start it before the fight.
Seraphine.escape: The moment after Seraphine E Beat Drop misses or is down is an opportunity to engage. Seraphine has no mobility spell, so she’ll have a hard time escaping if you close the distance and land Taric E Dazzle. Taric also has no spell to escape on his own, so don’t force an approach while Seraphine E Beat Drop is ready.
Seraphine.fight: Engage just after Seraphine E Beat Drop is down, when Seraphine is separated from her ranged damage dealer. Cast Taric E Dazzle in advance toward the spot where Seraphine will be a moment later. After landing it, use two basic attacks empowered by Taric P Bravado to shorten the cooldowns of your basic abilities.
Seraphine.laning: If there’s no opening to start a trade with Taric E Dazzle, don’t step forward; keep your distance. When Seraphine is near her allies, watch out for the range and damage of the empowered basic attack from Seraphine P Stage Presence, and look for an opportunity when she’s alone. After a trade, when using Taric P Bravado’s basic attacks on minions, choose a high-health target so you don’t take a last hit from your ranged damage dealer.
Seraphine.phase: In the mid to late game, protect allies with Taric W Bastion and time the activation of Taric E Dazzle and Taric R Cosmic Radiance.
Seraphine.teamfight: Spread out to the sides so your allies aren’t hit in succession by Seraphine R Encore. When Taric stands in front, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer to expand the area your abilities can reach. Taric R Cosmic Radiance can block damage but not crowd control such as charm, so cast it in advance before Seraphine R Encore hits.
Seraphine.watch: Seraphine E Beat Drop roots slowed targets and stuns immobilized targets, so if you’re slowed, move out of the straight line in front of her. Seraphine Q High Note deals more damage based on missing health, so be especially careful when health is low. In team fights, Seraphine R Encore gains range each time it hits an ally, so don’t line up.

Sona.build: Sona’s main damage is magic, so buy a Null-Magic Mantle first to build magic resistance. Choose Mercury’s Treads for boots.
Sona.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to the ally who will engage, then cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance. Next, stand slightly apart from your ally to narrow Sona’s room to dodge with the two beams from Taric E Dazzle, then follow up with two basic attacks from Taric P Bravado and Taric Q Starlight’s Touch. Account for Taric R Cosmic Radiance’s delay so its invulnerability overlaps with the trade after the stun.
Sona.escape: Look for an engage when Sona steps forward to apply an aura, before Sona E Song of Celerity activates. It’s a good time to engage after Sona R Crescendo is down, if you can land Taric E Dazzle. If Sona E Song of Celerity is active and she can retreat faster, avoid chasing too hard.
Sona.fight: When Sona steps forward to apply an aura or moves in to last-hit a minion, cast Taric E Dazzle in advance at the spot where she’ll be a moment later. If you land the stun, hit two empowered basic attacks from Taric P Bravado, heal with Taric Q Starlight’s Touch, and continue the trade. The key is to stun her before Sona E Song of Celerity lets her create distance.
Sona.laning: If there’s no good angle to cast Taric E Dazzle, don’t step forward and take poke. Use Taric P Bravado’s basic attacks while avoiding minions that are about to be last-hit, and save Taric Q Starlight’s Touch to build charges when healing isn’t urgent.
Sona.phase: Sona’s permanent growth stacks and recurring auras become more of a burden as time goes on, so use your early advantage.
Sona.teamfight: When Taric stands in front, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer to create two points from which your abilities can reach. Spread out to the sides so your allies aren’t all hit by Sona R Crescendo, and look for a stun with Taric E Dazzle when Sona steps forward. Disrupt Sona’s positioning by separating her from your group of allies to reduce the effect of her healing and shielding auras.
Sona.watch: When Sona approaches within basic attack range with Sona P Power Chord ready, watch for the empowered attack and slow, and create some distance. Sona R Crescendo is a straight-line stun, so don’t line up with your allies when Sona steps forward. Taric R Cosmic Radiance only blocks damage, so it won’t protect you from Sona R Crescendo’s stun.

Soraka.build: In the early game, hold on with a Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Soraka’s damage is mostly magic, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If healing makes fights drag on, consider Grievous Wounds next.
Soraka.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to the ally who will engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance, then aim Taric E Dazzle at the spot where Soraka will move. If the stun lands, hit two basic attacks from Taric P Bravado and heal with Taric Q Starlight’s Touch. Standing slightly apart from your linked ally lets Taric E Dazzle’s two beams cover a wider area.
Soraka.escape: The moment after Soraka E Equinox is used to poke or clear the wave is an opportunity to engage. Cast Taric E Dazzle before stepping into Soraka E Equinox’s area, then close the distance. Dodge Soraka Q Starcall so you don’t allow the slow or Soraka’s healing and movement speed increase.
Soraka.fight: When Soraka E Equinox is down, start a fight with Taric E Dazzle. Focus pressure on Soraka herself instead of continually attacking the ally she’s healing.
Soraka.laning: If there’s no opening to start a fight with Taric E Dazzle, don’t step forward and take ranged poke. If you land Taric E Dazzle on Soraka while she’s pressuring your allied ranged damage dealer, lowering her health also makes the health cost of Soraka W Astral Infusion a burden. You need to dodge Soraka Q Starcall to maintain that pressure.
Soraka.phase: In the mid to late game, armor items contribute both to Taric’s frontline role and damage, but when facing Soraka, prioritize magic resistance among your defenses.
Soraka.teamfight: Focus on Soraka herself instead of continually attacking enemies she’s healing. When Taric stands in front, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer; when he stands behind, link it to the ally who engages to expand the area your abilities can reach. Taric R Cosmic Radiance applies with a delay, so cast it in advance just before a fight or just after Taric E Dazzle, and keep in mind that invulnerability won’t block crowd control.
Soraka.watch: Soraka Q Starcall slows Taric, heals Soraka, and increases her movement speed, so dodge it. Soraka E Equinox can silence and root you, so cast your abilities before stepping into the area when you engage.

Thresh.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Thresh’s main damage is magic and Taric has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Taric’s bonus armor also increases the damage of Taric P Bravado and Taric E Dazzle, but it isn’t your first defense for enduring Thresh’s magic damage.
Thresh.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to the ally who will engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance. Then aim Taric E Dazzle at the spot where Thresh will move to stun him, follow with two basic attacks empowered by Taric P Bravado, and heal with Taric Q Starlight’s Touch. Standing slightly apart from your linked ally lets the two beams from Taric E Dazzle cover a wider area.
Thresh.escape: The moment after dodging Thresh Q Death Sentence is an opportunity to close the distance, but don’t rush in if Thresh W Dark Passage is still available. Plan the fight so Taric E Dazzle lands before Thresh W Dark Passage comes back up. Also avoid a position where Thresh E Flay can pull you in before you engage.
Thresh.fight: After dodging Thresh Q Death Sentence to the side, close the distance when Thresh W Dark Passage is also down. Cast Taric E Dazzle in advance toward the spot where Thresh will be a moment later, and if it lands, follow with two basic attacks empowered by Taric P Bravado. Taric’s main magic damage also lands well because Thresh has relatively low magic resistance.
Thresh.laning: Taric has no spell to escape on his own, so keep your distance while Thresh Q Death Sentence is ready, and change direction once more when moving out to last-hit. When Thresh walks forward to collect a soul, look for an opportunity to start a trade with Taric E Dazzle. Use Taric P Bravado’s basic attacks on high-health minions and other targets to cycle your abilities faster, but don’t take a last hit from your allied marksman.
Thresh.phase: In the mid to late game, Taric’s armor items contribute both to his frontline role and damage, but Thresh also becomes tougher as he collects souls.
Thresh.teamfight: When standing on the frontline, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer to use your abilities from two positions, and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance before damage piles up. Thresh Q Death Sentence and Thresh E Flay’s crowd control still work during invulnerability, so watch where your allies might be caught and aim Taric E Dazzle in advance. If you’re trapped in Thresh R The Box, choose a direction to break through and have your toughest ally break one wall so the rest can escape.
Thresh.watch: Thresh Q Death Sentence can lead from a stun into a dash, so move sideways when you see him raise his hook. Avoid the line between Thresh and his allies so Thresh E Flay doesn’t pull you toward his team. Taric R Cosmic Radiance can block damage but not crowd control, so cast it before the fight instead of waiting until you’ve been caught.

Velkoz.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Build magic resistance first against Vel’Koz’s main magic damage, but since resistance can’t block the true damage from Vel’Koz P Organic Deconstruction and Vel’Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray, your priority is to avoid getting hit by his abilities in succession.
Velkoz.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to the ally who will engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance. Then stun Vel’Koz at the spot where he’ll be a moment later with Taric E Dazzle, hit two basic attacks empowered by Taric P Bravado, and heal with Taric Q Starlight’s Touch. Standing slightly apart from your linked ally lets you spread the area covered by the stun beams from two positions.
Velkoz.escape: Vel’Koz has no mobility spell, so the moment after Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption is down is an opportunity to engage. When dodging Vel’Koz Q Plasma Fission, don’t only move sideways; move in toward Vel’Koz or out behind where the beam passed. If you get very close, Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption can knock you back, so find a spot to land Taric E Dazzle before engaging.
Velkoz.fight: When Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption is down, close the distance and start a trade with Taric E Dazzle. Don’t keep fighting from a spot where Vel’Koz has placed an ability telegraph; walk out of it.
Velkoz.laning: Don’t waste Taric E Dazzle on poke. Look for an opening when Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption is down or Vel’Koz moves in to last-hit a minion. If there’s no opening, don’t step forward and take poke. When using basic attacks to expend Taric P Bravado, choose a high-health minion so you don’t take a last hit from your allied marksman.
Velkoz.teamfight: When standing on the frontline, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer so Taric E Dazzle and Taric R Cosmic Radiance activate from two positions. Taric R Cosmic Radiance’s invulnerability applies with a delay, so cast it before damage piles up. If Vel’Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray begins, prioritize interrupting the channel with Taric E Dazzle.
Velkoz.watch: Dodge Vel’Koz Q Plasma Fission with its split beams in mind. If you’re hit by Vel’Koz W Void Rift and Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption in succession, Vel’Koz P Organic Deconstruction triggers true damage, so if you have stacks, back off and let them expire. When Vel’Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray begins, look for an opportunity to interrupt it with Taric E Dazzle.

Xerath.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Xerath’s damage is mostly magic, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Xerath.combo: Once Xerath’s stun and slow are down, link Taric W Bastion to the ally who will engage and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance. Then look for a stun with Taric E Dazzle, which also activates from your ally’s position, hit two basic attacks empowered by Taric P Bravado, and heal with Taric Q Starlight’s Touch.
Xerath.escape: The moment after Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are down is an opportunity to engage. You can also close the distance while dodging sideways as Xerath charges Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Xerath can’t move while casting Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, so you can engage on his position.
Xerath.fight: Close the distance just after Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are down. Xerath has no mobility spell, so aim Taric E Dazzle in advance at the spot where he’ll retreat. If it hits, use two basic attacks empowered by Taric P Bravado to cycle your basic abilities faster.
Xerath.laning: If there’s no opening to start a fight with Taric E Dazzle, don’t step forward and take Xerath’s poke. Hold on while avoiding his heavy damage, then push the lane and call your jungler when Xerath starts running out of mana. When using basic attacks to expend Taric P Bravado, choose a high-health minion so you don’t take a last hit from your marksman.
Xerath.phase: In the mid to late game, stand on the frontline and use Taric W Bastion to extend your ability range to an ally as well.
Xerath.teamfight: If you’re on the frontline, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer so your abilities activate from two positions. Anticipate Xerath’s attacks and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance, and aim Taric E Dazzle at where the enemy will be a moment later. Taric R Cosmic Radiance blocks damage but not stuns, so keep watching out for Xerath E Shocking Orb.
Xerath.watch: Dodge Xerath Q Arcanopulse by changing direction and moving sideways when you see him charging, since it passes through minions. Be especially wary of Xerath E Shocking Orb, as its stun can set you up for follow-up attacks. Also watch out for the slow from Xerath W Eye of Destruction and the area attacks from Xerath R Rite of the Arcane.

Zilean.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Zilean's damage is magic damage, so prioritize magic resistance. Tenacity is especially helpful when you're caught by the bomb stun and slow.
Zilean.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to the ally who is engaging and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance. Aim Taric E Dazzle from both positions at the spots where Zilean can move. Then land two Taric P Bravado attacks and heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Taric R Cosmic Radiance activates after a delay, so cast it before the fight starts, not after it becomes dangerous.
Zilean.escape: Zilean has no mobility, so once you close the distance and land Taric E Dazzle, you can stick to him and fight. If you go in alone, Zilean E Time Warp can catch you, so approach from a different direction than your allies.
Zilean.fight: If you land a stun, follow the ability with two Taric P Bravado attacks, then heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch as needed.
Zilean.laning: Don't waste Taric E Dazzle on poke. Aim it where Zilean will be standing shortly when he steps up to last-hit a minion. Use Taric P Bravado attacks on high-health minions to spend the charges and speed up your ability rotation. If early pressure fails and Zilean can use his bomb combo, farm outside bomb range.
Zilean.teamfight: When standing on the frontline, link Taric W Bastion to a backline damage dealer so Taric E Dazzle and Taric R Cosmic Radiance activate from both positions. Taric R Cosmic Radiance can block damage but not stuns, so stay away from allies with Zilean Q Time Bomb attached. Instead of using your abilities on an enemy affected by Zilean R Chronoshift, wait for its duration to end or target them right after they revive. If neither is viable, target the squishy Zilean himself.
Zilean.watch: Zilean Q Time Bomb stuns when two bombs attach, so move away from allies as soon as the first bomb attaches and get outside the blast radius.

Zyra.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Zyra deals mostly magic damage, and Taric has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Zyra.combo: Link Taric W Bastion to the ally who is engaging and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance in advance. When Zyra E Grasping Roots is down, land Taric E Dazzle. Then land two empowered Taric P Bravado attacks and heal with Taric Q Starlight's Touch. Taric R Cosmic Radiance blocks damage after a delay but doesn't block crowd control, so also dodge the areas of Zyra E Grasping Roots and Zyra R Stranglethorns.
Zyra.escape: The window to engage opens after Zyra E Grasping Roots misses. Zyra has no mobility, so close the distance then and land Taric E Dazzle. Taric also has no ability to escape on his own, so don't force your way into an area covered by plants.
Zyra.fight: Close the distance when Zyra E Grasping Roots is down and there are no plants nearby. Zyra has no mobility, so account for Taric E Dazzle's delay and place the stun in her path. After it hits, land two empowered Taric P Bravado attacks after each ability.
Zyra.laning: If there's no opening to start a trade with Taric E Dazzle, don't step forward; dodge Zyra E Grasping Roots first. Step on seeds to remove them when it's safe, but back off if Zyra tries to grow them with an ability. If plants have grown, retreat briefly and trade after they disappear.
Zyra.phase: In the mid to late game, stand on the frontline, but move the fight away from areas where Zyra has stockpiled seeds.
Zyra.teamfight: Don't take a fight in an area where Zyra has had plants set up for a long time; move elsewhere to fight. When Taric is on the frontline, link Taric W Bastion to a backline ally to extend your ability range, and cast Taric R Cosmic Radiance before damage lands. When Zyra R Stranglethorns' indicator appears, move outside its area so you don't spend your invulnerability time knocked up.
Zyra.watch: If Zyra E Grasping Roots catches you, you're likely to take the follow-up plant damage and get knocked up by Zyra R Stranglethorns. Move sideways at the edge of range to dodge the root. When you see Zyra R Stranglethorns' cast indicator, walk out of its area, and don't fight where her plants have gathered.
